findings.claim: The span helper in score.sh does split("-") | map(tonumber). The committed corpus entry R5 has defect.lines "89-" (an open range, corpus.json:18). That splits to ["89",""], and tonumber on "" is a jq error. So `score.sh R5` aborts with a jq error and exit 1, and prints neither the case header nor any located finding. R5 is one of the 23 real cases, so the committed scorer cannot score it, and the fixture test only uses closed ranges so it does not catch this. Either R5's lines must be a closed range, or span must accept a trailing '-'.

run-gentle.sh reuses out/<id> across reruns without clearing it. A rerun that ends without an approved or correction_required capture (a status stop, or four rounds without a result) still reads the earlier run's out/final.json and any stale cap<round>-*.json. The summary then pairs the new state with the old lenses and findings, and score.sh would score those stale findings. The script also reports no error when a case ends with an empty state. For a harness whose numbers set the C25 bar this can silently corrupt a recall figure. Fix: remove final.json and cap*.json (or the whole out/<id>) before starting.
proof_refs: tools/review-bench/run-gentle.sh: mkdir -p "$out" with no cleanup; cp "$f" "$out/final.json" only on a terminal state; final.json is slurped unconditionally in the summary jq

findings.claim: The shim creates a mktemp stdin copy and a .out file in $BENCH/scratch for every reviewer process and never removes them. A full corpus run leaves about 46 files of roughly 33-41 KB each plus the outputs. The shim also fails without a clear message when $BENCH/scratch does not exist, because run-gentle.sh creates only out/<id>.
proof_refs: tools/review-bench/shim/claude: in="$(mktemp -p "$bench/scratch")" with no trap or rm
